nodes.label: DDG vs Serper Engine Routing
nodes.rationale: ddgs ignores site:/OR/quoted operators; operator queries must route to --engine serper or they underperform.

nodes.label: Relay Fraud / 跑路 Denylist
nodes.rationale: Commercial 中转 relays risk exit-scam and 降智 (silent model downgrade); durable free access lives in first-party platforms and BYOK OSS routers.

nodes.label: Curated Free-LLM GitHub Targets
nodes.rationale: Auto-refreshed awesome-list repos safe to ingest via github_adapter; reaches prod today since the worker runs github every 6h.

nodes.label: LLM Aggregator Landscape (proposed wiring)
nodes.rationale: Snapshot of 'one key, many models' services; proposes new deep_web query templates and github_adapter targets, not yet applied.

nodes.label: Proposed Aggregator Query Templates
nodes.rationale: New (category_tag, query) tuples for deep_web_adapter, split by DDG-safe vs Serper-only (site:/OR/quotes) engines.

nodes.label: Ingest→Normalize→Verify→Dedup→Dispatch Pipeline
nodes.rationale: One orchestrator turns raw_items into offers and hands them to the dispatcher; each stage is isolated so one bad item never kills a run.

nodes.label: Server-only DB Credentials
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL never leaves the server; browser talks only to API routes, guarded by a read-only role, LIMIT caps, and a 5s statement timeout.

nodes.label: Exact + Semantic Dedup
nodes.rationale: sha256 URL/title hashes catch exact dups; app-side cosine over local embeddings catches near-dups (threshold 0.92).

nodes.label: Idempotent Atomic Dispatch
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE(offer_id, channel) + a claimed_at lease guarantee no double-sends across re-runs or concurrent workers.

nodes.label: Local Dev Stack (Postgres + Redis)
nodes.rationale: docker-compose mirrors Heroku's topology: Postgres 16 for the offer store, Redis 7 for rate buckets and dedup scratch.

nodes.label: Manual Ingest Fallback
nodes.rationale: Facebook is not scraped; a manual paste form / CLI inserts raw_items under a manual source, reusing the same pipeline with zero legal surface.

nodes.label: Pydantic v2 Offer Schema
nodes.rationale: Strict schema validates/normalizes every LLM extraction: enum fallbacks, currency casing, tz-aware expiry, confidence bounds.

nodes.label: Rate Safety & Backoff
nodes.rationale: Dispatcher paces under Discord 30 msg/min and honors 429 Retry-After; LLM extractor retries 429/5xx with backoff.

nodes.label: App-side REAL[] embeddings (no pgvector)
nodes.rationale: Heroku Postgres lacks pgvector, so embeddings are stored as REAL[] and computed app-side; acceptable under 10k rows. AWS/Docker path can use pgvector HNSW instead.

nodes.label: AWS Free Tier Fallback
nodes.rationale: Same architecture on a different substrate at ~$0/mo; only revisited if Heroku Postgres mini is outgrown or a pgvector HNSW index is needed. Main traps are NAT Gateway (~$32/mo), detached EIP, and second instances.

nodes.label: Heroku Config Vars (secrets)
nodes.rationale: Secrets kept out of git: DATABASE_URL (manual Neon), REDIS_URL (add-on), LLM_* keys required for extraction, DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL, TG_* (blank skips adapter), FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, PROXY_URL, GITHUB_TOKEN, DASHBOARD_API_KEY.

nodes.label: Dashboard to PostgreSQL secure path
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL never leaves the server side; Next.js reads DB only in server components/API routes with a pg Pool. Browser talks to API routes with LIMIT/OFFSET caps, read-only SQL roles, and a 5s statement timeout.

nodes.label: Heroku Architecture (primary deploy target)
nodes.rationale: Heroku is primary because $290.28 platform credits make it effectively free for ~19 months, and the US region runs outside the local ISP network to bypass local Telegram blocks.

nodes.label: Heroku Redis (mini add-on)
nodes.rationale: 100 MB mini plan at $5/mo used for rate-limit token buckets, dedup bloom scratch, and session cache; REDIS_URL is injected by the add-on.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres (permanent existing DB)
nodes.rationale: Neon is the permanent DB holding live raw_items, offers, dispatches, sources, runs. DATABASE_URL is set manually to the Neon pooler URL; provisioning heroku-postgresql would orphan live production data, so it is explicitly forbidden.

nodes.label: Deployment Security Checklist
nodes.rationale: Secrets only in config vars, .gitignore covers .env/*.state.json/sessions/; dedicated disposable Telegram account; Discord webhook treated as secret; Scheduler commands pinned to repo module paths (no shell strings); AWS Budgets alarm mandatory.

nodes.label: Web Process (Next.js dashboard)
nodes.rationale: Kept unscaled (web=0) until the Phase 4 dashboard exists; scaling it up would burn dyno hours for nothing.

nodes.label: torch + sentence-transformers (omitted for Heroku)
nodes.rationale: Intentionally omitted because torch + sentence-transformers exceed Heroku's 500 MB slug limit. Pipeline degrades gracefully: verifier._load_st_model() returns None, embed() returns None, dedup falls back to exact SHA-256 URL hashing.

nodes.label: Normalized Adapter Payload Contract
nodes.rationale: Every adapter emits one identical JSON shape stored verbatim in raw_items.raw_payload, so downstream code is source-agnostic.

nodes.label: Telegram Flood Discipline
nodes.rationale: MTProto user-account client, sequential 1 req/1-2s, 50 msgs/channel/run, FloodWait capped at 15min; a banned account is a service incident.

nodes.label: Stealth Tarpit Breaker
nodes.rationale: A login wall / px-captcha trips a breaker that screenshots, disables the identity 24h, and alerts — never auto-solve CAPTCHAs.

nodes.label: Crash-safe Watermark Resume
nodes.rationale: channel_cursors(last_message_id) is bumped only after a batch is fully persisted, so a crash resumes without gaps or dupes.

nodes.label: Eco Dynos (1000 h/mo shared pool)
nodes.rationale: Eco dynos sleep on inactivity, but a slot fires every ~53 min (MINUTES_PER_SLOT=53.33) with 18.8 min of continuous ingest work, so the dyno is never idle long enough to sleep. Escalation is scheduler=1:standard-1x if sleeping bites.

nodes.label: Scheduler Process (27-slot orchestrator)
nodes.rationale: The single always-on process; supersedes worker because the 27-slot orchestrator runs every ingest adapter plus the pipeline plus dispatch in-process, dropping the ~45h of former one-off jobs to 0h. Runs 744h/mo = 74% of the 1000h Eco pool.

nodes.label: Worker Process (Telegram realtime monitor)
nodes.rationale: Scaled to 0 and commented out (not deleted) so it stays recoverable; its only unique function was the Telegram realtime monitor, which is credential-dead (blank TG_*) and now degrades to a logged skip. Running it alongside scheduler would be ~1488h and exceed the Eco pool.

nodes.label: APScheduler (27-slot scheduler)
nodes.rationale: Backs the 27-slot scheduler with a SQLite job store; SQLAlchemy is its dependency for the job store.

nodes.label: ddgs (renamed DuckDuckGo search, preferred)
nodes.rationale: ddgs is the renamed package used preferentially; duckduckgo-search is kept only for environments that have not upgraded yet.

nodes.label: firecrawl-py 4.38.0 (pinned exact)
nodes.rationale: Pinned exactly to 4.38.0 because the code depends on the V1FirecrawlApp / V1JsonConfig signature.
